combat_history.event: Vietnam fields Bastion-P batteries for South China Sea coastal defence; Russia has used the system in a land-attack role in Syria and Ukraine.
combat_history.significance: A regional sea-denial capability in ASEAN hands.

modernization.description: Coastal anti-ship missiles spreading among regional states.
modernization.impact: Densifies sea-denial threats around contested waters.

vulnerabilities.description: Long-range shots need off-board over-the-horizon targeting.
Supersonic cruise is detectable before terminal sea-skim.

operational_patterns.typical_deployment: Concealed mobile coastal batteries holding warships at risk near a defended coastline.
operational_patterns.readiness_notes: Fielded by Vietnam and others; mobile and concealable.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: China's coastal supersonic anti-ship missile; the Bastion-P is the system regional states use against Chinese ships.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: The coastal-missile contest in the South China Sea.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: BrahMos derives from the same P-800 Oniks; both are supersonic anti-ship missiles, BrahMos multi-platform.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: From Oniks to BrahMos to Bastion.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: The NSM (on NMESIS) is the Western mobile coastal anti-ship missile; the Bastion is the supersonic Russian equivalent.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: Coastal anti-ship missiles East vs West.

doctrine.role: Mobile coastal-defence missile system for shore-based sea denial against naval task groups.
doctrine.employment: Concealed truck launchers fire supersonic P-800 Oniks salvos on over-the-horizon cueing, then relocate.
doctrine.design_philosophy: Let a smaller power impose cost and risk on larger navies from concealed mobile launchers.
doctrine.threat_context: Centrepiece of Vietnam's South China Sea sea-denial against Chinese naval action.
doctrine.comparison_frame: Read against China's YJ-12, the related BrahMos and the Western NSM/NMESIS.
